set.typical_award_size: Gap loans sized by the joint City and County Multi Family Transaction Underwriting Guidelines (Jan 21, 2020). Minimum award $100,000, no set maximum. Fund balance at June 30, 2026 was $6.3 million unaudited, of which $2.4 million was formally reserved for specific projects; FY 2025-26 fee collections were about $1.2 million, and $3.1 million of impact fees plus Homekey+ funds acquired the 24 unit 4th and Division Apartments that year (FY 2025-26 draft CAPER). Prior year: $8.7 million balance with $5 million reserved at June 30, 2025. Track record: $2.2 million general fund plus trust fund money each to Heritage House (90 units, 40 PSH) and Valley Lodge (54 units PSH) in 2022; four projects held reservations from the impact fee and TOT funds at the time of the 2023 Prohousing application. set.typical_award_size: Special tax of 1% on hotel and short term rental stays (TOT raised from 12% to 13%), effective January 1, 2019, dedicated solely to affordable and workforce housing projects, programs and services in the City of Napa. FY 2025-26 revenue about $2.5 million; fund balance at June 30, 2026 about $8.9 million unaudited, of which only about $264,000 was formally reserved for a specific project (FY 2025-26 draft CAPER), so most of the balance is uncommitted. The $3.7 million committed in 2021 and 2022 to the Crescent ownership project (15 moderate and 25 low income units, construction started summer 2026) was expended in Program Year 2025. Prior year: $10.2 million balance with $4 million reserved and $2.8 million revenue (FY 2024-25 CAPER). Measure F campaign estimate was $2.1 million a year. Awards are low or no interest deferred loans under the same rolling NOFA as the impact fee fund.

set.next_deadline: Fee due before building permit issuance, or deferred under a recorded secured building agreement (Government Code 66007) to final inspection or certificate of occupancy, whichever occurs first; the City routinely defers fees for affordable projects to occupancy. Developers may propose an alternative equivalent proposal (on or off site affordable units, land dedication, conversion of market rate units, preservation) with City Council approval under 15.94.070. A petition for reduction, adjustment or waiver under 15.94.100 must be filed with the City Clerk at least 10 days before the first public hearing on the discretionary approval, or within 10 days after paying the fees under protest if no discretionary approval is required. A developer contesting the Director's fee determination for an unlisted nonresidential use has 30 days under 15.94.040(E).
set.audit_note: City spot check Nov 9, 2026: next_deadline said 15.94.100 petitions must be filed within 30 days of the fee determination; code says 10 days before the first public hearing (or 10 days after payment under protest), and the 30 day window applies only to contesting a Director fee determination under 15.94.040(E). Fee schedule ($4.05 multifamily, $4.75 single family and condo, $3.55 office and retail, $6.00 hotel, $3.50 industrial) reconfirmed on the City rate sheet.

reason: Fee schedule and exemptions match, but the code sets a 10 day filing window for 15.94.100 waiver petitions, not 30 days.
